concerns.text: Tasks T056–T062 implement 'Admissible Question Language' (AQL), 'Knowledge Gap Verification', and 'Productive Ignorance' metrics. These tasks enforce 'origination control' and 'bias mitigation' mechanisms that directly contradict the spec's core philosophical constraint (Problem Statement) which explicitly rejects 'self-teaching' and 'origination' in favor of 'negative selection on belief'. Implementing these tasks would violate the constitutional principle that the system is an engine executing ordered operations, not an originator of knowledge.

Task T014a generates critiques using 'deterministic templates' for structure, while Task T056 (Phase 8) mandates an 'AQL Engine' mapping internal states to 'pre-ordained question templates' to prevent origination. These are mutually exclusive generation mechanisms for the same data (dialogue tuples). The spec defines the critique as the selection signal (FR-002), not the question generation process. T056 introduces a new, unapproved methodology (origination control) that conflicts with the approved T014a approach, creating an unresolvable implementation conflict.

Task T033 specifies performing 'Paired t-tests'. The plan.md (Complexity Tracking) explicitly rejects this approach, stating 'Paired t-tests are invalid as the models and training sets are distinct' and mandates 'Independent Samples t-tests'. Executing T033 as written violates the approved methodology and would produce statistically invalid results, failing FR-006's requirement for rigorous comparison.

Tasks T001a and T001b create directory structure and `requirements.txt` at the repository root. The Constitution (Principle I) and plan.md (Project Structure) explicitly require the code to reside under `projects/PROJ-582-socratic-transformers-dialogue-based-sel/code/`. This task violates the Single Source of Truth and Reproducibility constraints by placing artifacts in the wrong location, breaking the defined project structure.

Task T021 requires implementing a hard assertion that RSS < 7GB using `psutil`. The plan.md (Compute Feasibility & Escape Hatch) relies on the 'execution stage' to detect OOM and trigger a Kaggle GPU fallback. A hard assertion in the script will cause a crash before the execution stage can intercept the error, effectively disabling the approved GPU escape hatch mechanism and violating the CPU-First strategy's fallback logic.

Task T014a describes generating critiques via templates but omits the 'Critic Model confidence score > 0.6' requirement mandated by the Constitution (Principle VII) and plan.md (Constitution Check). Without this explicit logic in the task, the generated data may fail the Adversarial Dialogue Quality Gate, violating the requirement to discard non-adversarial data.
